papers.title_en: From Documentation to Zero-day Vulnerabilities: LLM-Driven Fuzzing of JavaScript Engines in PDF Readers
papers.authors: Suyue Guo, Stijn Pletinckx, Tianle Yu, Yigitcan Kaya, Saad Ullah, Wenbo Guo, Christopher Kruegel, Giovanni Vigna
papers.evidence: LLM驱动的软件漏洞检测模糊测试
papers.tldr: 现有PDF阅读器模糊测试仅依赖简单API调用，难以覆盖需多步骤交互的复杂漏洞场景。针对此问题，本文提出PDFuzzer，利用大语言模型从JavaScript API手册与执行轨迹中自动构建上下文无关语法、推断API调用间依赖关系，并借助约束求解器生成具体调用序列。在Adobe Acrobat Reader、Foxit PDF Reader和PDF-XChange Editor上，PDFuzzer相比现有工具覆盖率最高提升48%，发现包括信息泄露到任意代码执行的31个零日漏洞，并获厂商安全奖励，充分验证了LLM驱动模糊测试的实用价值。
papers.abstract_en: Existing fuzzers for PDF readers rely on simple test cases that involve only individual API calls, leading to limited coverage and potentially missing vulnerabilities that require sequences of API calls. To address these limitations, we propose PDFuzzer, a novel PDF engine fuzzer that automatically generates complex and meaningful API call sequences. PDFuzzer first uses a Large Language Model (LLM) to construct context-free grammars and infer the relationships between individual API calls from specifications extracted from JavaScript API manuals and execution traces. Based on the grammars and relationships, PDFuzzer employs a constraint solver to generate concrete API call sequences for fuzzing. Our experiments show that PDFuzzer significantly outperforms state-of-the-art PDF fuzzers (TypeOracle, Favocado, and Cooper) and LLM-based fuzzers (Fuzz4All, naive LLM) on three mainstream PDF readers: Adobe Acrobat Reader, Foxit PDF Reader, and PDF-XChange Editor. PDFuzzer achieves up to 48% higher coverage than existing tools and identifies 31 zero-day vulnerabilities in these readers, from information leakage to arbitrary code execution. Our ablation study validates the necessity of each component, including LLMs, which achieve high accuracy across all pipeline stages (93-98%). We disclosed all vulnerabilities to the vendors via a coordinated vulnerability disclosure process and received bug bounties.

papers.title_en: Dissecting Software Graphs: Structural Insights for Driver-Guided Fuzzing
papers.authors: Baihong Chen, Hua Ming, Weifeng Pan, Tian Xie, Haipeng Cai, Wen Li
papers.evidence: 多驱动程序模糊测试的动态分析，结合静态图结构优化漏洞发现
papers.tldr: 多驱动程序模糊测试的效率取决于执行模式，但现有评估多关注覆盖率。本文提出以静态调用图为骨架、投影驱动动态覆盖的子图抽象，并设计四阶段方法分析27个C/C++项目。结果显示多驱动优于最佳单驱动，覆盖节点和边显著提升，但驱动贡献不均，子图结构差异大，未探索区域呈规律模式。
papers.abstract_en: Many software systems expose multiple execution modes through command-line options, subcommands, and configuration flags. For such programs, fuzzing depends on both mutated inputs and the invoked mode. Yet evaluations still focus on coverage and bug counts, leaving unclear how execution modes partition, overlap, and miss software structure, and how these differences affect effectiveness. We present an empirical study of software structure under multi-driver fuzzing. We propose a structural abstraction that uses a static call graph as a shared backbone and projects driver-specific dynamic coverage onto it to derive driver-induced subgraphs. Based on this abstraction, we develop a four-phase methodology for backbone construction, fuzzing and profiling, graph-based analysis, and research-question-driven evaluation. We apply it to 27 OSS-Fuzz-derived C/C++ projects, spanning 43 executables and 854 driver configurations. Under the same total budget, multi-driver fuzzing outperforms the best single-driver baseline, increasing covered call-graph nodes by 27.9% and CFG-edge coverage by 73.5%, and revealing 11 unique bugs and abnormal behaviors largely missed by single-driver fuzzing. However, driver contributions are uneven, subgraphs differ substantially in cohesion, fragmentation, modularity, overlap, and residual under-exploration follows recurring regimes rather than a homogeneous tail. These results show that multi-driver fuzzing is fundamentally a structural exploration problem.

papers.title_en: Smart Contract Invariants Protect Against Cybercriminals
papers.authors: Sofia Bobadilla, Humaira Afrin, Angela Novelli, Martin Monperrus
papers.evidence: 利用程序不变量防御真实智能合约漏洞利用，属于漏洞利用防御
papers.tldr: 区块链是极端对抗环境，智能合约漏洞导致巨额加密资产被窃，常见防护手段效果有限。本文提出以程序不变量作为核心防护机制，构建INVARIANTEVAL基准（含28个真实以太坊攻击）和PONDEREPLAY重放框架，用于系统验证不变量能否阻断攻击。实验结果表明，人工编写的28条不变量全部有效，经108,637笔历史交易重放验证正确，证明不变量可有效防御智能合约网络犯罪。
papers.abstract_en: Blockchains are among the most adversarial environments in computing. Billions are stolen by cybercriminals who exploit vulnerabilities. This is an open problem and no concept or technique has proven to really make a difference. In this paper, we claim that the classical notion of program invariant is perhaps the most powerful solution to the problem. We devise anoriginal experimental protocol to 1) study how invariants would have protected against past real-world attacks and 2) whether state-of-the-art automated tools can find them. The experimental toolchain is sophisticated. It is based on INVARIANTEVAL, a benchmark of 28 real Ethereum exploits, each paired with a human-authored invariant that blocks the attack. We validate every invariant with PONDEREPLAY, a replay framework that re-executes transactions in order to prove the correctness and soundness of smart contract invariants. We demonstrate that smart contract invariants block all the cybercriminal attacks in INVARIANTEVAL, fully validated by replaying 108,637 historical transactions. Our large-scale experiments clearly demonstrate that smart contract invariants protect against cybercriminals.

papers.title_en: A Lightweight Fault-Detection Scheme for Barrett Modular Multiplication Using Multiple Conditional Reduction Paths
papers.authors: Rourab Paul, Paresh Baidya, Krishnendu Guha, Amlan Chakrabarti
papers.evidence: 面向 Barrett 模乘的硬件故障检测，防御侧信道与硬件木马
papers.tldr: 格基后量子密码（PQC）和全同态加密（FHE）中的多项式乘法广泛使用Barrett模乘（BMM），但BMM单元易受侧信道攻击、硬件木马及老化等因素引入的故障影响，威胁系统安全。本文提出统计约简监控（SRM）方法，利用多条件约简路径实施轻量级故障检测。该方法在最小硬件开销下，可高效检测随机故障和突发故障，有效防止信息泄露。为PQC和FHE基础设施中的关键模块提供了低成本高可靠性的防护方案。
papers.abstract_en: Polynomial multiplication is the most resource-, time-, and energy-critical operation in lattice-based Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) and Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) schemes. Lattice-based PQC schemes such as Kyber and Dilithium have already been standardized, while lattice- based FHE schemes such as BGV, BFV, and CKKS are widely recognized as leading candidate in FHE area. Barrett Modular Multiplication (BMM) for polynomial multiplication is widely adopted in PQC and FHE hardware accelerators due to its hardware friendly nature and efficient modular reduction capabilities. However, Side-Channel Attacks (SCAs) and Hardware Trojans may introduce intentional faults, while aging and various other factors can cause unintentional faults. These faults may target the BM M unit, one of the most critical components of PQC and FHE infrastructures, potentially leading to information leakage and compromising system security. In this paper, we employ a Statistical Reduction Monitoring (SRM) method to protect the BM M unit against such adversarial conditions. papers.title_en: Synchronous Observers Revisited for Runtime Verification of Lustre Using STL
papers.authors: Logan Kenwright, Partha Roop, Sobhan Chatterjee, Nathan Allen
papers.evidence: 将STL编译为同步观测器以支持运行时的动态验证
papers.tldr: 信号时序逻辑(STL)是运行时验证中广泛使用的形式化语言，而同步语言通常用同步观察者表达安全属性，但很少将其用于在线监控。针对这一空白，本文提出将STL同步片段(SSTL)编译为Lustre同步观察者的方法，通过模块化编译支持任意嵌套的有界SSTL属性，并允许全局无界的外层算子用于在线监控。生成的观察者既可直接运行时验证，也可作为副产品用于Kind2模型检查器的静态验证；还提供了交互式可视化器，可在可编辑轨迹上显示三值判定，并在弹簧-质量系统和跟车巡航控制器两个案例中验证了有效性。
papers.abstract_en: Signal Temporal Logic (STL) is a popular formalism for the temporal safety properties of cyber-physical systems, most often used for runtime verification. In the synchronous family of languages, safety properties are instead expressed as synchronous observers, modules composed with a program for static verification, which are also runnable specifications suitable for runtime verification, though this use is rarely explored. We present a technique for compiling the synchronous fragment of STL (SSTL) into synchronous observers in the dataflow language Lustre. Unlike previous work, we allow arbitrary nesting of bounded SSTL properties via modular compilation, and admit a globally unbounded outer operator for online monitoring; the resulting observers serve both runtime verification and, as a by-product, static verification with the Kind2 model checker. We further contribute an interactive visualiser that renders a property's three-valued verdict over an editable trace, and evaluate on two case studies from the literature: a spring-mass system and a car-following cruise controller.
